facts.text: The Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table (EMESRT) is a group of mining companies that writes shared safety requirements for mining-machine manufacturers; its PR-5A requirement addresses collisions between vehicles and people and supplies a nine-layer control model and collision scenario catalog.
facts.quote: EMESRT is a group of mining companies that writes shared safety requirements for the makers of mining machines, and PR-5A is its requirement for controlling collisions between vehicles and people

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: Large mining companies formed EMESRT to speak with one voice to equipment manufacturers about design-related safety problems.
facts.quote: was formed by large mining companies to speak with one voice to equipment manufacturers about design-related safety problems.

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: EMESRT is an industry body, not a regulator; its documents are a risk-control philosophy, not law or proof that a product passes a mine's acceptance test.
facts.quote: It is an industry body, not a regulator; its documents are a "risk-control philosophy, not law, and not proof that a product passes a mine's acceptance test"

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: EMESRT requirements shape mining customer demands worldwide because mining fleets mix machines from multiple manufacturers with third-party detection systems.
facts.quote: Because mining fleets mix machines from many makers with third-party detection systems, EMESRT's requirements shape what mining customers ask for worldwide.

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: Performance Requirement PR-5A, Vehicle Interaction Systems, exists in Rev 1.0 (April 2016), Rev 2.0 (August 2019, with a version dated 2 September 2019), and Rev 3.0 (September 2024, as cited in a vendor white paper).
facts.quote: It exists in Rev 1.0 (April 2016), Rev 2.0 (August 2019, a version dated 2 September 2019) and Rev 3.0 (September 2024, as cited in a vendor white paper)

facts.text: PR-5A defines nine vehicle interaction control levels: site requirements, segregation controls, operating procedures, authority to operate, fitness to operate, operating compliance, operator awareness (Level 7), advisory controls (Level 8), and intervention controls (Level 9).
facts.quote: site requirements, segregation controls, operating procedures, authority to operate, fitness to operate, operating compliance, operator awareness (Level 7), advisory controls (Level 8) and intervention controls (Level 9)

facts.text: In the PR-5A control model, Levels 1–7 are the site's own defenses, Level 8 warns, and Level 9 takes control from the operator to slow or stop the machine.
facts.quote: Levels 1 to 7 are the site's own defenses; Level 8 warns; Level 9 slows or stops the machine.

facts.text: EMESRT and its partners insist that Level 9 intervention is not a standalone product but a machine-control capability resting on a strong Level 1–7 baseline.
facts.quote: EMESRT and its partners insist that "Level 9 intervention is not a standalone product" but a machine-control capability resting on a strong Level 1 to 7 baseline

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: PR-5A describes surface vehicle interaction scenarios as storyboards, including following on straight roads and curves, overtaking, head-on encounters, junctions, congested dump and park areas, and light vehicles interacting with heavy equipment.
facts.quote: "storyboards": following on straight roads and curves, overtaking, head-on, junctions, congested dump and park areas, light vehicle against heavy equipment and so on.

facts.text: The booklet records conflicting PR-5A scenario counts without resolving the difference: a 2019 trade article reports 24 scenarios, whereas EMESRT's 2024 Activity Report reports 17 published surface storyboards.
facts.quote: 24 scenarios according to a 2019 trade article and 17 published surface storyboards according to EMESRT's own 2024 Activity Report, and it does not resolve the difference

facts.text: An agricultural research paper describes PR-5A as a replicable model for operational design domain (ODD) definition and validation.
facts.quote: An agricultural research paper calls PR-5A "a replicable model for ODD definition and validation", ODD meaning operational design domain

facts.text: PR-5A supplies the only sector-specific scenario list and the control vocabulary used by mining customers.
facts.quote: PR-5A supplies the only sector-specific scenario list and the control vocabulary that mining customers use

facts.text: The booklet maps the project's requirements and scenario catalog to PR-5A storyboards and South African MOSH numbers as the most concrete acceptance targets available.
facts.quote: the booklet maps the project's requirements and scenario catalog to the PR-5A storyboards and the South African MOSH numbers as "the most concrete acceptance targets available"

entities.name: Mining Industry Occupational Safety and Health learning hub

facts.text: PR-5A's nine-layer model warns against validating automatic braking in isolation from roadway design, segregation, procedures, and advisory controls.
facts.quote: Its nine-layer model also warns against validating the brake in isolation from roadway design, segregation, procedures and advisory controls
